newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels kill at least 10 soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels kill at least 10 soldiers.

text.p: Leftist rebels killed 10 soldiers in fighting in northwest Colombia, including four gunned down early on Thursday at a military base that was overrun and reduced to rubble, authorities said.

Military spokesmen said most of the 28 soldiers at the Heroes de Barbacoas counterinsurgency base in a mountainous area about 40 miles (65 km) east of Medellin, the capital of Antioquia province, were asleep when a 150-strong guerrilla force launched a blistering attack at about 1:30 a.m.

The rebels overran the base and destroyed it with a combination of rocket-propelled grenades and dynamite, the spokesmen said. They said four soliders were killed in the attack, four were wounded and two were listed as missing.
Six other soldiers have been killed in fighting raging since Tuesday in the banana-growing region of Uraba in the northwest corner of Antioquia near the border with Panama.

Thursday's assault on the military base was carried out by a combined force of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas, both Marxist-led groups founded in the 1960s.

Interior Minister Carlos Holmes Trujillo was to hold talks with provincial Gov. Alvaro Uribe Velez in Medellin later in the day to discuss what the governor has described as the rapidly deteroriating public security situation in Antioquia.

Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri said Colombia's "very painful war of attrition" was being won by the government, not the rebels. "The authorities are out there working all the time, taking prisoners and fighting (rebel) columns," he said.
"More than 400 (rebels) have been killed in the first half of the year," he added. "The guerrillas have never suffered so many deaths before."
